question: Which Portuguese Governor started the 'Blue Water' policy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Francisco De Almeida**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The "Blue Water" policy was initiated by Portuguese Governor Francisco de Almeida during his tenure in the early 16th century**__. 

 __
 
• He was appointed as the first Portuguese Viceroy of the Estado da Índia (State of India) in 1505 by King Manuel I of Portugal.
 
• **The Blue Water policy **was a strategic maritime doctrine that aimed to establish Portuguese naval supremacy in the Indian Ocean and protect Portuguese trade and shipping from Arab and Turkish naval attacks. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Portuguese **(1498) were 1st company that came to India with Vasco da Gama who had discovered the sea route to India via Cape of Good Hope(Africa).
 
• The **Dutch **East India Company came in 1595.
 
• **English **East India Company came to India in 1600.
 
• The **Danish **East India Company came to India in 1616.
 
• **French **East India Company was the last company came to India in 1664.
